rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads the phrase as ‘provision for their wives’; Abu Ubayd notes that analogous Quranic expressions commonly appear in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: ويذرون أزواجا متاع لأزواجهم، قال أبو عبيد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative متاعا is a verbal noun, with an implied command to provide for them.
rows.anchor: متاعا نصب على المصدر أي متعوهن متاعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation takes the provision as something God has made for the widows.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جعل الله عز وجل ذلك لهن متاعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other analyses make متاع accusative as a circumstantial accusative or attach it to the bequest, by analogy with feeding an orphan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصب على الحال، وقيل: نصب بالوصية كقوله أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision is a year of food, clothing, housing, or other needs, provided she is not expelled; غير إخراج may be a circumstantial phrase or mean ‘without expulsion’ with a preposition understood.
rows.anchor: والمتاع: النفقة سنة لطعامها وكسوتها أو سكناها أو ما تحتاج إليه إلى الحول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسائر المفسرين
rows.claim: They report that the verse came after Hakim ibn al-Harith of al-Taif died in Medina, leaving parents, children, and a wife; the Prophet gave inheritance to the parents and children and ordered a year’s support for the widow.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وسائر المفسرين: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من أهل الطائف يقال له: حكيم بن الحرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the earlier custom, a widow stayed in her husband’s home for a year with support from his estate, received no inheritance, and lost support if she left; men made a bequest for this arrangement.
rows.anchor: وكان سكناها ونفقتها واجبة في مال زوجها هذه السنة ما لم تخرج

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line about widows whose year has lengthened is cited as poetic evidence for the year-long mourning custom.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: والمرملات إذا تطاول عامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance rulings abrogated the widow’s year of estate support, replacing it with a quarter or an eighth, and 2:234 replaced the year-long waiting period with four months and ten days.
rows.anchor: فنسخ الله نفقة الحول بالربع والثمن، ونسخ عدة الحول بقوله يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If widows leave voluntarily before the year ends, the deceased’s guardians incur no blame; ‘what is recognized’ means seeking marriage.
rows.anchor: فإن خرجن يعني من قبل أنفسهن قبل الحول من غير إخراج الورثة فلا جناح عليكم يا أولياء الميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular أحد is used after بين rather than آحاد because أحد can refer to one person or a group; the verse, a hadith, and Ru'bah’s line illustrate the usage.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال (بين أحد) ولم يقل آحاد لأن الآحاد يكون للواحد والجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ ‘we hear and obey’ contrasts with the Jews’ response.
rows.anchor: وقالوا سمعنا. قولك وأطعنا. أمرك خلاف قول اليهود

rows.speaker: حكيم بن جابر
rows.claim: He reports that Gabriel came when ‘The Messenger believes’ was revealed, said God had favored the Prophet and his community and invited him to ask, and the Prophet asked for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وروى حكيم بن جابر أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين نزلت آمن الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غفرانك is an accusative verbal noun with an omitted verb, as in سبحانك.
rows.anchor: وهو نصب على المصدر أي أغفر غفرانك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes the response to mean ‘we ask You for forgiveness.’
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه: نسألك غفرانك

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers an implicit plea about what the believers have been required to bear: God requires of a soul only what it can manage.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية قضاء الحوائج، وفيها إضمار السؤال والحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وسع is what a person can encompass or manage; another gloss connects it with what is difficult and strenuous.
rows.anchor: والوسع: اسم لما يسع الإنسان

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة الشامي
rows.claim: He reads وسعها with fatḥa on waw and kasra on sin as a verb, meaning God’s command encompassed the soul, or ‘what encompassed it’ with ما omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة الشامي: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: ابن عطاء والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: They say this answered believers’ fear that they could not repent of involuntary inner thoughts after 2:284; such thoughts exceeded their capacity.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عطاء والسدي وأكثر المفسرين: أراد به حديث النفس

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another account, the verse concerns believers specifically: God eased religious duties and required only what they can do, as shown by verses affirming ease, no hardship, and duty according to capacity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية أخرى: [ ... ] المؤمنون خاصة وسع الله عليهم أمر دينهم

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan glosses capacity as ease rather than hardship: God did not require the soul’s full strength, since that would exhaust it; al-Tha'labi calls this a good view because capacity is below full ability.
rows.anchor: فقال: إلا يسرها لا عسرها، ولم يكلفها طاقتها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الكلام
rows.claim: Some theologians understand the phrase as only requiring what is lawful and within a person’s permitted scope.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض أهل الكلام: يعني إلا ما يسعها ويحل لها

words: لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds belong to the soul with their reward, while its evil deeds and their burden are against it.
rows.anchor: لها ما كسبت. أي للنفس ما عملت من الخير والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تؤاخذنا means ‘do not punish us.’
rows.anchor: ربنا لا تؤاخذنا. لا تعاقبنا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Although the verb is in a reciprocal form, it describes one actor: the sinner has effectively opened a way for the punisher and thus shares in the taking to account.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: وإنما خرج على لفظ المفاعلة وهو فعل واحد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view reads forgetting literally; al-Kalbi explains that Israelites were punished when they forgot or erred, with foods or drinks forbidden in proportion to the offense, and believers were taught to ask for exemption.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا نسوا شيئا مما أمروا به وأخطئوا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view understands forgetting as abandoning or neglecting; al-Tha'labi prefers the literal sense, though he cites 9:67 for the alternative usage.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو من النسيان الذي هو الترك والإغفال.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take أخطأنا as deliberate intention, using خطيء for someone who sins intentionally; a line by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: جعله بعضهم من القصد والعمد، يقال: خطيء فلان إذا تعمد

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Others take it as unintentional ignorance or oversight, which al-Tha'labi calls more correct because deliberate sin is not automatically forgiven, though it remains subject to God’s will unless it is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وجعله الآخرون من الخطأ الذي هو الجهل والسهو وهو الأصح لأن ما كان عمدا من الذنب غير معفو عنه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata glosses the phrase as ‘if we were ignorant or did it deliberately.’
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: إن نسينا أو أخطأنا. يعني إن جهلنا أو تعمدنا له

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd applies forgetting to neglecting a required duty and error to doing something forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إن نسينا شيئا مما افترضته علينا

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that Umar corrected a man’s prayer for forgiveness of his errors, saying errors are forgiven and he should ask forgiveness for deliberate acts.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: سمع عمر رجلا يقول: اللهم [اغفر] لي خطاياي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that error, forgetfulness, and what people are coerced into have been lifted from his community.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما أكرهوا عليه»

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والضحاك والربيع ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي وابن جريج والفراء
rows.claim: This group glosses إصر as an unbearable covenant or pledge, whose breach brought punishment on earlier people, especially the Jews; they cite 3:81’s use of إصر for a covenant.
rows.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والضحاك والربيع ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي وابن جريج والفراء

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبو عبيدة والمؤرخ والقتيبي وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Another group glosses إصر as a burden or severity and asks that burdens like those imposed on the Jews not be laid on believers; examples include fifty prayers, alms on profits, cutting away impurity, and sins displayed at the door. They connect it to 7:157.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول عثمان بن عطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبي عبيدة والمؤرخ والقتيبي وابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the plea is not to impose a sin for which there is no repentance or expiation; the word can also mean a tie or bond.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معناه: لا تحمل علينا ذنبا ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can name what binds things together, a kinship bond, or a relationship formed by covenant; the cited poem uses آصرة for such a tie.
rows.anchor: ويقال للشيء الذي تعقد به الأشياء: الأصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem’s آصرة is evidence for the word’s sense of a bond or tie between people.
rows.anchor: إذا لم تكن لامرئ نعمة

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They take the plea to mean: do not require deeds beyond our ability.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكلفنا من الأعمال مالا نطيق، هذا قول قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view applies the phrase to inner speech and whisperings.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو حديث النفس والوسوسة

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim, in a report from Sufyan al-Thawri through Mansur, glosses it as hardship.
rows.anchor: سفيان الثوري عن منصور عن إبراهيم في قوله تعالى ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به. قال: المشقة

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab interprets the unbearable burden as passionate love.
rows.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الوهاب ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به. قال: يعني العشق

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab recounts that eleven people died during a gathering where Dhu al-Nun al-Misri spoke of divine love and its overpowering effects on lovers.
rows.anchor: قال خباب: حضرت مجلس ذي النون المصري في فسطاطه

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yahya says he would not punish lovers because their sins arise from compulsion rather than choice.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى: لو تركت العقوبة بيدي يوم القيامة ما عذبت العشاق

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the unbearable burden with transformation into apes and swine.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: هو مسخ القردة والخنازير

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that enemies gloat over the afflicted person.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو شماتة الأعداء.

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that Job said the hardest part of his long affliction was his enemies’ gloating.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد المنعم بن إدريس عن أبيه عن وهب بن منبه قال: قيل لأيوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preceding, now-unattributed gloss identifies the referent as Abu Bakr; the excerpt begins mid-discussion, so its precise antecedent is not preserved.
rows.anchor: يعني: أبا بكر. قال الباقون: آل إبراهيم: إسماعيل

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining commentators identify Abraham’s family as Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and say Muhammad belongs to both Abraham’s and Imran’s families.
rows.anchor: قال الباقون: آل إبراهيم: إسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies Imran as son of Yashhar, son of Fahat, son of Levi, son of Jacob, and his family as Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو عمران بن يصهر بن فاهاث بن لاوي بن يعقوب وآله موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: الحسن ووهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Hasan and Wahb ibn Munabbih identify Imran as a descendant of Solomon and David, and his family as Mary and Jesus.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن ووهب بن منبه: هو عمران بن أشهم بن أمون من ولد سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account names Imran ibn Matan and his wife Hanna, and says this family was singled out because prophets and messengers descended from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عمران بن ماتان ، وامرأته حنة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses ذرية as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ذرية: نصب على حال قاله الأحفش

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses it as an accusative by interruption, since ذرية is indefinite while the named families are definite.
rows.anchor: الفراء على [القطع] لأن الذرية نكرة وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران معرفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses ذرية as an appositive.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: نصب على البدل

rows.speaker: قيل وأبو روق
rows.claim: Other parses take ذرية as an indefinite noun or a circumstantial accusative meaning that some descended from others; Abu Rawq says they shared one religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على النكرة أي اصطفى ذرية بعضها من بعض: وقيل: على الحال أي بعضها من ولد بعض. وقال أبو روق: بعضها على دين بعض

rows.speaker: الحروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi recounts that when Hasan al-Basri died on a Friday evening, nearly everyone followed his funeral and the Basra congregational mosque had no one left for the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الحروي: لما مات الحسن البصري وكان مماته عشية الجمعة

rows.speaker: الجزائري
rows.claim: Al-Jaza'iri says he heard a caller proclaim that God selected Hasan al-Basri above the people of his time.
rows.anchor: قال الجزائري: سمعت مناديا ينادي: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران

rows.speaker: الأعمش عن أبي وائل
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reports that Abu Wa'il read the verse from Ibn Masud’s codex with the wording إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران.
rows.anchor: الأعمش عن أبي وائل، قال: قرأت في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say this is Imran ibn Ma'yan, not Moses’ father Imran; the two lived 1,300 years apart, and Ma'yan’s descendants were Israelite leaders, scholars, and kings.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومقاتل: هو عمران بن مايان وليس هو بعمران أبو موسى

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives Imran’s genealogy as a descendant of Solomon and David.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق : هو عمران بن أشهم بن آمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanna says she has made the child in her womb devoted to God; a vow is something a person obligates themself to, conditionally or unconditionally.
rows.anchor: والنذر: ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه بشريطة كان ذلك أو بغير شريطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Mary’s ‘I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast,’ نذرت means ‘I obligated’; the same sense appears when someone vows another’s blood.
rows.anchor: إني نذرت للرحمن صوما : أي أوجبت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever vows obedience to God must fulfill it, while whoever vows disobedience must not fulfill it.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من نذر أن يطيع الله فليطعه

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha’s line uses نذرت النذورا as a poetic example of making a vow.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: غشيت لليلي بليل خدورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom نذر فلان دم فلان means that he imposed on himself the duty of killing the person.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قولهم: نذر فلان دم فلان: أي أوجبت على نفسه قتله

rows.speaker: جميل
rows.claim: Jamil’s line about men who vowed his blood likewise illustrates the verb نذر.
rows.anchor: وقال جميل: فليت رجالا فيك قد نذروا دمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محررا means freed, pure, and wholly devoted to God as a servant of the sanctuary, withdrawn from worldly concerns; related usage describes an emancipated slave, a corrected text, an unfettered person, or pure clay.
rows.anchor: محررا: أي عتيقا خالصا لله خادما للكنيسة حبيسا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محررا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ومحررا: نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: الكلبي وابن إسحاق وغيرهما
rows.claim: They describe the Jerusalem sanctuary custom: a consecrated boy served there until puberty, then could choose to stay; if he stayed, he could not leave. Boys alone were assigned because girls were thought unsuitable due to menstruation and impurity.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي وابن إسحاق وغيرهما: فإن الحر رجل إذا حرر وجعل في الكنيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says Hanna, childless into old age, saw a bird feeding its young and prayed for a child, vowing to dedicate it to Jerusalem as a caretaker in gratitude; she became pregnant without knowing the child’s sex, worried a girl could not serve, and Imran died while Hanna was pregnant.
rows.anchor: وكان القصة في ذلك أن زكريا وعمران تزوجا أختين، وكانت إيشاع بنت فاقود أم يحيى عند زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary from Hanna and approved her in place of the consecrated boy; the verb can mean to accept what one approves. Some instead understand the acceptance as undertaking her care.
rows.anchor: فتقبلها: أي تقبل الله من حنة مريم ورضيها مكان المحرر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الكسائي والأئمة
rows.claim: They explain قبول as the verbal noun with fatḥa, an exceptional form whose expected pattern would have ḍamma, like دخول and خروج.
rows.anchor: والقياس الضم مثل الدخول والخروج، قاله أبو عمرو الكسائي والأئمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say God’s acceptance meant that He undertook Mary’s upbringing and care.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى التقبل: التكفل في التربية والقيام بشأنها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says God accepted Mary by never punishing her at any time, day or night.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: قبوله إياها أنه ما عذبها ساعة من نهار ولا ليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording بقبول حسن uses a verbal noun of a different form from the verb; al-Farra compares it to تكلمت كلاما, with poetry offered as parallel usage.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع يقال له: المصدر على غير المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase continues the verbal-noun pattern with نباتا after أنبتها.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: مثل قولك تكلمت كلاما.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guided Mary among the blessed and formed her without excess or defect; she grew in a day as much as an ordinary child grows in a year.
rows.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن يقول

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God nourished and provided for Mary until she matured into a full adult woman.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج: أنبتها ربها في غذائه ورزقه نباتا حسنا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say Hanna carried newborn Mary to the sanctuary and presented her to the priests, who contested guardianship because she was the daughter of their imam and keeper of offerings; they agreed to draw lots, and twenty-nine men went to a flowing river.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: أخذتها أم مريم حين ولدتها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the river where they cast lots as the Jordan.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: هو نهر الأردن، فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others say Zakariyya’s pen rose above the water while the others sank.
rows.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا فوق الماء وانحدرت أقلامهم [ورسبت] في النهر، قاله ابن إسحاق وجماعة

rows.speaker: السدي وجماعة
rows.claim: An alternative account says Zakariyya’s pen stood upright as if fixed in clay while the others flowed away with the water, so he won the lot.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وجماعة: بل ثبت قلم زكريا وقام فوق الماء كأنه في طين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya, their chief priest and prophet, took Mary into his household and assumed her care.
rows.anchor: وكان رأس الأحبار ونبيهم فذلك قوله تعالى: وكفلها زكريا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zakariyya placed Mary with her maternal aunt, Yahya’s mother, arranged a wet nurse, then built her a chamber in the mosque with a high entrance accessible only by a ladder; he brought her food, drink, and oil daily.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فلما كفلها زكريا ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى

words: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision was fruit out of season: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, fresh and ripe.
rows.anchor: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا: يعني وجد زكريا عندها فاكهة

words: هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Mary was asked about the provision God gave her, she answered that it came from God, who provides without measure.
rows.anchor: فإنها كانت إذا رزقها الله شيئا وسألت عنه قالت هو من عند الله

words: هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب
rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that, after days without food, the Prophet visited Fatima; she had none, but a neighbor later sent bread and meat. Fatima saved it for him despite her family’s hunger, and the covered dish was miraculously full; she used Mary’s words, and the Prophet praised her resemblance to the leader of Israelite women.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا عبد الله بن حامد بإسناده عن جابر بن عبد الله: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام أياما

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s reading softens the shin and opens the ba; this form of بشر يبشر is a Tihama dialect, and poetry is cited for it.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن مسعود. قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي حماد
rows.claim: Reporting from Muadh al-Kufi, he distinguishes the intensified form as giving glad tidings and the lighter form as making joyful; a report from Ibn Zayd and his father supports the latter sense.
rows.anchor: روي عبد الرحمن بن أبي حماد عن معاذ الكوفي، قال: من قرأ يبشرهم مثقلة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam reports from his father that the Prophet told a man God was giving him the good news of a boy, and the man’s wife gave birth to a boy.
rows.anchor: ما روى ابن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified form from بشر يبشر is, in al-Tha'labi’s view, the most correct and eloquent; Jareer’s line and other Quranic forms support it.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتشديد من بشر يبشر بشيرا وهو أعرب اللغات وأفصحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is indeclinable as a proper name, has an augmented initial syllable like Yazid, Ya'mur, and Yashkur, and is read with either imala or tafkhim; its plural is يحيون.
rows.anchor: بيحيى: هو اسم لا يجري لمعرفته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Yahya was so named because God gave life to his barren mother’s womb through him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لأن الله أحيا به عقر أمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says he was named Yahya because God enlivened his heart with faith.
rows.anchor: قتادة: لأن الله أحيا قلبه بالإيمان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God enlivened Yahya’s heart through prophethood.
rows.anchor: بعضهم: لأن الله أحيا قلبه بالنبوة

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: Hasan ibn al-Fadl says Yahya was named for living in obedience, never sinning or even intending sin.
rows.anchor: الحسن بن الفضل: لأن الله أحياه بالطاعة حتى لم يعص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet the report that everyone meets God having intended or committed a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن ابن عباس، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما من أحد إلا ويلقى الله

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم بن حبيب
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi’s teacher says Yahya was named for being martyred, since martyrs are alive and provided for by their Lord.
rows.anchor: قال الثعلبي: [سمعت] الأستاذ أبا القاسم بن حبيب يقول: سمي بذلك لأنه استشهد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says it shows how little the world means to God that a woman killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من هوان الدنيا على الله إن يحيى بن زكريا قتلته امرأة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ refers to the accounts of Zakariyya, Yahya, Mary, and Jesus; the pronoun in نوحيه refers back to that account, and الغيب means reports of the unseen.
rows.anchor: ذلك: الذي ذكرت من حديث زكريا ومن حديث ويحيى ومريم وعيسى

words: وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not present when they cast lots to decide who would care for Mary; the lots were arrows or drawing-sticks, with قلم as the singular.
rows.anchor: وما كنت: يا محمد، لديهم: عندهم، إذ يلقون أقلامهم سهامهم وقداحهم للاقتراع في الماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the objects cast into the water were their pens for writing the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: [أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها] التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispute was over who would take responsibility for Mary.
rows.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون: في كفالتها

rows.speaker: أبو السماك وهب بن يزيد العدوي
rows.claim: He reads كلمة with kasra on kaf and a jussive lam throughout the Quran, a fluent dialect like كتف and فخذ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السماك وهب بن يزيد العدوي: (بكلمة) مكسورة الكاف مجزومة اللام
